items.title: Name the emotion first
items.core: If you can name it, you will be less likely to be held hostage by half.
body: Use specific words to describe: anxiety, grievance, shame.
Distinguish between emotions and facts.
Use "I feel..." to make sentences and turn vague and uncomfortable feelings into specific emotional words, such as grievance, anxiety or shame.
Create a list of emotions in your mobile memo, check them immediately when emotions appear, and slowly form your own recognition vocabulary.
Take two minutes every day before going to bed to reflect on a strong emotion, name it accurately and write it down.

Case: A colleague refuted Xiao Li’s plan in a meeting. He suddenly felt tight and wanted to fight back immediately. He stopped and said in his mind, "This is frustration." He did not refute immediately. Instead, he took a deep breath and communicated after class. He found that the other party was just adding details.

items.title: Separate thoughts from facts
items.core: The judgments in your mind are not equal to what happened.
body: Write down facts, speculation, and unknowns.
Find counterexamples to the speculation.
Take a piece of paper and write down your thoughts in the left column, and only write the objective facts you see in the right column. Compare and distinguish them one by one.
Add the prefix "I guess" to your thoughts to remind yourself that this is only a subjective interpretation and does not equal the truth.
When making a negative judgment, first ask yourself "What evidence do I have?" If you can't find it, don't draw a conclusion.

Case: Xiao Wang sent a message to a friend and did not reply for a long time. "The other person hates me" popped into his mind. But he looked through the chat history and found that his friend was just busy on a business trip, so he put aside his speculations and waited until he received a reply in the evening.

items.title: Emotions are not instructions
items.core: Just because you feel strong doesn't mean you have to act on it.
body: Acknowledge your feelings first.
Then decide whether to act.
When you feel emotional, first silently say "This is just a feeling, not an action instruction" and give yourself a buffer for ten seconds.
Write down the impulsive action you want to do most at the moment, and then write down two more mild alternative actions for you to choose from.
Practice delayed reactions, save the messages you want to send in your drafts, and check again the next day to see if you still need to send them.

Case: Xiao Zhou was very angry when his neighbor cut in line and wanted to accuse him in public. He told himself that "anger is a signal, not a command", walked away a few steps and took a drink of water, and then calmly reminded the other person that he apologized and moved to the back of the queue.

items.title: Record trigger points
items.core: Recurring stimuli tend to have patterns.
body: Take note of the time, scene, and physical reactions.
Look back and find common ground.
Prepare a small notebook and write down the time, place, people present and what just happened every time your emotions fluctuate.
Go through your records every week, look for recurring scenes or characters, and mark high-frequency triggers.
After discovering the pattern, design small changes, such as changing routes and preparing in advance, to gradually reduce the chance of triggering.

Case: Xiao Chen feels depressed as soon as Sunday night comes, and has been like this for several consecutive weeks. She recorded her trigger points and found that most of them occurred when she thought about Monday’s regular meeting. She prepared the report outline in advance, and her anxiety on Sunday was significantly reduced.

items.title: Allow emotions to exist
items.core: Suppression often makes it last longer.
body: Give yourself some non-judgmental time.
Breathe or write with it.
Don’t rush to cheer up when you feel uncomfortable. Say to yourself “I can be sad for a while” and give space to your emotions.
Set a short period of time, such as twenty minutes, and concentrate on feeling your emotions without using your phone to distract your attention.
Use a pen to write "I allow myself to feel..." and turn depression into a sense of acceptance.

Case: Xiao Zhao felt panicked after the project failed, but he kept telling himself "don't be pretentious". Later, he allowed himself to feel uncomfortable and sat in the park for half an hour. After crying, he calmed down and resumed the test smoothly the next day.

items.title: Pay attention to body signals
items.core: Emotions are often reflected in the body first.
body: Pay attention to your heartbeat, shoulders, neck and stomach.
Record the scene.
When you are feeling uncertain, scan your body: forehead, shoulders, stomach, palms of your hands to find any tightness or abnormalities.
If you find yourself feeling tight, exhale slowly three times, deliberately relax the corresponding muscles, and let your body relax first.
Record the correspondence between body signals and emotions, for example, stomach tightening is anxiety, and gradually build self-awareness.

Case: Before Xiao Lin gave a report, his palms were sweating and his shoulders were tight, and he realized that he was very nervous. He slowed down his breathing, relaxed his shoulders, and stabilized his voice after taking the stage, and the report was successfully completed.

items.title: Rate emotional intensity
items.core: Quantification can reduce the feeling of being overwhelmed.
body: Mark on a scale of 1 to 10.
Observe when the peak occurs.
Rate your current emotions from 0 to 10. First determine the value, and then see if you are overwhelmed.
Stop communication if it exceeds 6 points, and wait until the intensity drops below 4 points before dealing with difficult topics.
Record similar emotional scores for several consecutive days, observe the trend, and discover what things bring you close to the high score.

Case: Xiao Sun became very angry after an argument with his partner. He rated his anger at 8 points and found that it was almost at its peak. He first went to the balcony to calm down and talk again half an hour later. The conflict did not escalate and the two of them explained the problem clearly.

items.title: Set a time limit for emotions
items.core: The emotions that spread infinitely are the most consuming.
body: Agree a period of time to focus on your feelings.
When the time comes, do a small thing.
When emotions arise, clearly write down an end time, such as "Resolve this grievance before nine o'clock tonight."
Do a specific small thing within the time limit, such as writing three sentences about your feelings or taking a walk, to give your emotions an outlet.
After reaching the point, take the initiative to switch activities, such as listening to music or taking a bath, and use actions to tell yourself that the emotional period is over.

Case: Xiao Wu was depressed all day after being criticized. He set a time limit for his emotions to be "sorted out before leaving get off work", wrote a note to remind himself, put the note away after the time limit, and returned to his normal state at night.

items.title: Distinguish between needs and ideas
items.core: Ideas may not be facts.
body: Write down “what I need”.
Mark the speculation separately.
Rewrite the "I should" sentence pattern into "I need" to distinguish external requirements from your own real needs.
Ask "Is this really what I want" three times in a row to screen out ideas that are internalized by other people's standards.
List the three most energy-consuming things this week, and mark the core needs that are not being met behind each thing.

Case: Xiao Zheng feels exhausted because “I have to satisfy everyone”. When writing the list, he found that what he really needed was rest and recognition, so he declined to work extra overtime. After catching up on sleep on the weekend, his condition improved a lot.

items.title: Recognizing Shame
items.core: Shame often disguises itself as procrastination.
body: Say “I don’t feel like I’m good enough.”
Separate it from the truth.
When procrastination occurs, ask yourself "What evaluation am I afraid of?" and find out the hidden shame.
Say to yourself "I'm not good if I don't do well" and separate evaluation from self-worth.
First make a rough version within five minutes, and use completion to break the stagnation caused by shame.

Case: Xiao He always puts off handing in his homework because he thinks he is lazy. Later he realized that he was afraid that he would be laughed at if he could not write well. This was due to his sense of shame. He wrote a rough first draft, slowly revised it, and finally submitted it on time.

items.title: Behind anger there are often needs
items.core: Anger indicates that boundaries have been touched.
body: Ask yourself what was violated.
Speak out your needs.
When you are angry, ask yourself "Which of my boundaries has been touched?" and translate the anger into specific needs.
Use "I need..." to express your demands instead of using accusations to make it easier for the other party to accept.
Record the needs corresponding to each anger, such as respect and fairness, and slowly figure out your bottom line list.

Case: Xiao Liu got angry because his colleagues always asked him to help. After calming down, he realized that he felt used. He made it clear that "we are tight this week and cannot help." The other party understood and the relationship became more comfortable.

items.title: Record successful coping experiences
items.core: Evidence is needed when you are at low points.
body: Write down how you got through the past.
Keep reusable methods.
Create a "coping evidence" document, and write down the specific actions you took every time you successfully overcome a difficulty.
Record the time, dilemma, and three things done right to make the evidence details clear and reusable.
When you feel down, open the document and read it. Pick an approach that has worked before and try it today.

Case: When Xiao Tang was at his lowest point, he looked through his records and saw that he had gotten out of his depression by walking in the morning and chatting with friends. He did so, and a week later his mood improved and he truly felt "I've been through this before."

items.title: No need to rush to solve it
items.core: Stabilize first and then deal with it.
body: Allow yourself a moment.
Wait until the mood subsides before deciding.
When you feel emotional, physically leave the scene for a few minutes and tell yourself, 'This matter can be dealt with later.'
Use a pen to write down the strongest feelings and thoughts at the moment, shifting your attention from impulsive reactions to objective records.
Set yourself a cooling-off period, such as 'in an hour' or 'tomorrow morning', and then revisit the problem after it expires.

Case: Xiao Zhang was questioned about the plan by his colleagues at the meeting, and his heartbeat accelerated. He didn't refute immediately, but said, 'I'll record it and reply later', and then went to the tea room to drink a glass of water. Ten minutes later, I calmed down and came back to respond in an organized manner, thus avoiding conflict.

items.title: Allow ambivalence
items.core: It's normal to like and hate something at the same time.
body: There is no need to force unified feelings.
Write both sides separately.
When conflicting emotions arise, try saying 'I feel A and B at the same time' instead of 'What's wrong with me'.
Visually accept this complexity by drawing an emotional spectrum line, marking the proportion of each opposing feeling.
Write the conflicting feelings on paper. List the reasons why you like it on the left and the reasons why you hate it on the right. After reading, fold it and put it away.

Case: When Li Wei was sorting out her old things, she found a gift from her ex-boyfriend. She smiled as she recalled the good times, but felt her heart tighten again. Instead of forcing herself to choose one or the other, she put the gift in the box and put it away, allowing both feelings to exist at the same time.

items.title: Naming subtle emotions
items.core: The more precise it is, the easier it is to process.
body: From "annoyance" to "disappointment".
Use specific words to express.
When you feel uncomfortable, first ask, 'Is this anger, disappointment, shame, or grievance?' and replace the general feeling with more precise words.
Record the details of physical reactions, such as 'a tight stomach means anxiety', 'a hot face means embarrassment', and establish a connection between body and mind.
Use an accurate word to describe the strongest emotion of the day before going to bed every day, and stick to it for a week to improve your recognition ability.

Case: Wang Ming felt depressed after receiving the leader’s revised opinions. He didn't say 'I'm angry', but wrote 'the feeling of shame after being rejected' in the memo on his mobile phone. After naming it, he discovered that what he was afraid of was that his ability would be questioned, not just anger.

items.title: Emotion is not identity
items.core: You are not an emotion itself.
body: Start with "I feel now."
Don’t take feelings as conclusions.
Change 'I'm very anxious' to 'I feel anxious at the moment', and replace the word 'is' with the word 'have' to create greater psychological distance.
Imagine the emotions are the clouds in the sky and you are observing the clouds in the sky and silently say 'This is the emotion, not me' three times.
Make a 'Me vs. Emotions' comparison table. Write your stable traits on the left and the names of fluctuating emotions on the right.

Case: Chen Chen had insomnia for three consecutive days because of the project failure, thinking 'I am a loser'. The counselor asked her to write on paper 'I feel a sense of failure' instead of 'I am a failure'. She realized that her emotions were only temporary states and began to focus on remedies.

items.title: Observe trigger frequency
items.core: Recurring stimuli appear regularly.
body: Record time, people and events.
Look back at the commonalities.
Prepare an emotional logbook and write down the time, place, people present and preceding events for each fluctuation.
Review the records every Sunday and look for recurring keywords, such as 'at the meeting again' or 'late night again'.
When high-frequency trigger points are identified, try making small adjustments first, such as changing the way you speak or changing the ambient light.

Case: Liu Fang found that she was always depressed on Sunday nights. After two weeks of recording, she discovered that she started to feel anxious every time after checking next week’s schedule. So she changed her plan to Saturday afternoon, completely relaxed on Sunday, and her mood improved significantly.

items.title: Build your own emotional vocabulary
items.core: The richer the vocabulary, the less likely it is to be confused.
body: Remember an emotional word every day.
Used for real feelings.
Create an 'emotion favorite' in your mobile memo. When you encounter unfamiliar emotional words, look up the meaning and write down your own related experiences.
Choose a precise emotional word every week, such as 'sadness', recall a corresponding scene and describe the physical feeling.
Put the emotional words next to the mirror and choose a word before going out every day to predict the emotions you may encounter today.

Case: Zhao Min could only say 'annoyed' before. She started recording the "Emotional Dictionary" and when she read the word 'grieved', she immediately remembered her experience of being queue-jumped. Now she can differentiate between 'irritable' and 'suffering', the latter of which makes her more aware of the need to maintain boundaries.

items.title: Breathing is the fastest landing exercise
items.core: Prolonged exhalation can slow down the body.
body: Breathe in slowly and exhale longer.
Repeat a few rounds before taking care of things.
Use the 4-7-8 breathing method: inhale for 4 seconds, hold your breath for 7 seconds, exhale slowly for 8 seconds, repeat three times to calm down quickly.
Set the exhalation time to twice the inhalation time, such as inhaling for 3 seconds and exhaling for 6 seconds, to immediately reduce physiological arousal.
When you are nervous, pretend to blow out a candle, exhale slowly with slightly pouted lips. This prolonged exhalation can activate the parasympathetic nerves.

Case: Sun Lei’s palms were sweating before the interview. He secretly used the 4-7-8 breathing method: inhale for 4 seconds, hold the breath for 7 seconds, and exhale for 8 seconds. After three rounds, my fingers were no longer cold and my voice had stabilized. This exercise allowed him to switch from panic to focus.

items.title: Sleep is the base of emotions
items.core: Long-term lack of sleep will amplify all fluctuations.
body: Fixed wake-up time.
Reduce stimulation one hour before bed.
Turn the bedroom into a dedicated space for sleeping, remove the TV and office supplies, and strengthen the conditioned reflex between bed and rest.
Do a fixed routine one hour before going to bed: turn off the main light, dim the desk lamp, change into pajamas, and don’t touch your phone to give your body a signal to fall asleep.
If you sleep less than 6 hours for three consecutive days, take the initiative to cancel non-essential social interactions and prioritize getting more sleep to restore your emotional foundation.

Case: Zhou Ting went to bed at two o'clock in the morning for a week in a row. She was extremely sensitive to colleagues' jokes during the day and even cried. After two days of catching up on sleep, she found that the same thing didn't make her sad at all. Lack of sleep reduced her ability to regulate her emotions by at least half.

items.title: Get your body moving
items.core: Movement can change the chemical environment of your mood.
body: Start with a ten-minute walk.
Choose the intensity you can persist with.
When you are emotional, do jumping jacks or raise your legs in place for 5 minutes to quickly release the body’s stress chemicals.
Choose rhythmic exercise such as brisk walking or swimming, and follow the movements with your attention to interrupt the negative thinking cycle.
Set up 'movement trigger clothing' and put on that set of clothing whenever you feel irritable to establish conditioned reflexes for actions and emotions.

Case: Wu Lei was frustrated after being rejected by the client. He put on his running shoes and went downstairs for a brisk walk for 20 minutes. After sweating out, the recurring thoughts of 'I can't do this' in my mind began to fade away. By the time he got home, he had the energy to revise his plan.

items.title: Reduce Rumination
items.core: Thinking about the same thing over and over does not lead to new information.
body: Write ideas into questions.
Limit a thinking time.
Set a 'dedicated period' for rumination, and tell yourself 'write it down and think about it later' when thoughts come up at other times.
Use 'then what' to ask yourself: If you think about this again and again, what specific actions can you take next? Cut off idling.
When you find yourself ruminating, immediately do something that requires hand-eye coordination, such as typing or chopping vegetables, to force your attention away.

Case: Mr. Zheng Hao repeatedly wonders why his ex left, even though he knows there is no answer. He sets 17:00-17:15 as his 'exclusive rumination time' every day, and when other thoughts come up, he tells himself 'I'll think about it later'. The rumination time naturally shortened after two weeks.

items.title: Basing in the sun and eating regularly
items.core: Basic rhythm affects emotional stability.
body: Exposure to natural light during the day.
Don’t rely on overeating to regulate.
Open the curtains or stand outside for 5 minutes within an hour after getting up, allowing the sunlight to calibrate the biological clock and increase serotonin.
Breakfast contains protein and complex carbohydrates, such as eggs and oatmeal, to avoid blood sugar fluctuations and exacerbating mood swings.
Set three fixed meal alarms and eat small portions even if you are not hungry. Maintaining stable blood sugar equals stable mood.

Case: Lin Xiao was always depressed in March. Later, she found out that she only drank coffee for breakfast and did not see sunlight all day long. She changed to eating eggs and milk every day and taking a 15-minute lunch break to soak up the sun. After two weeks, I felt significantly less tired and irritable in the afternoons.

items.title: A fixed wake-up time
items.core: ​​is more effective than a fixed bedtime.
body: Don’t make too much difference on weekends.
Expose yourself to light after getting up.
Set a fixed wake-up time throughout the year, with an error of no more than 30 minutes, including weekends and holidays.
If you stay up late last night and still start at the original time that day, you will feel sleepy early in the evening, which will naturally bring your rhythm back.
Expose yourself to sunlight or turn on bright lights as soon as you wake up to send a clear signal to your brain that 'day has begun'.

Case: He Wei used to catch up on sleep until noon on weekends, but always felt groggy on Mondays. He changed to getting up at 7 o'clock every day, including weekends. It was painful at first, but after a week I felt naturally sleepy at night, fell asleep faster, and the drowsiness during the day completely disappeared.

items.title: Schedule activities during the day
items.core: Physical activity helps you fall asleep at night.
body: It doesn’t have to be intense.
Avoid strenuous exercise before going to bed.
Walking briskly for 20 to 30 minutes in the morning or afternoon at an intensity that allows you to speak a complete sentence but not sing.
Get up for 3 minutes every 60 minutes after sitting for long periods of time. Do squats, stand against a wall, or go to the window to get some sunshine.
Only do low-intensity exercises such as stretching or yoga in the evening, and avoid strenuous exercise before going to bed.

Case: After lunch break, she walked briskly in the community for twenty minutes, and basked in the sun for another ten minutes. She stopped tossing and turning when she lay down after taking a bath at night, and fell asleep within half an hour.

items.title: Reduce caffeine intake
items.core: Affects sleep after the afternoon.
body: Pay attention to personal sensitive times.
Reduce gradually rather than stop suddenly.
Put coffee, strong tea and energy drinks in the morning as much as possible, and record the time of the last intake.
Look at the ingredient list to identify caffeine. Milk tea, cola and some functional drinks are also included in the total amount.
If you are slow to fall asleep, palpitation, or wake up at night, try half the amount for a week, and then observe changes in sleep.

Case: Xiao Li felt sleepy at three o'clock in the afternoon. He used to drink latte instead of drinking warm water and walking for five minutes. After a week, the number of times he woke up at night dropped from two or three times to once.

items.title: Write down to-dos before going to bed
items.core: Get thoughts out of your head.
body: Just write the first step tomorrow.
Put it down after you finish writing.
Write three columns on paper before going to bed: Must do tomorrow, can be postponed, and need to wait for other people's reply.
Write each specific action starting with a verb, such as 'send an email to confirm the time' instead of 'project'.
After finishing writing, close the notebook and put it in a fixed location. Do not open the memo to add new tasks.

Case: While lying in bed, she kept thinking about the materials she needed to hand in and the courier she needed to pick up the next day, so she wrote down three things on a note and put it in the hallway. The number of thoughts over and over again in her head was obviously reduced.

items.title: Practice lengthening your exhales
items.core: Exhales are longer and more relaxing than your inhales.
body: Inhale for a count of four and exhale for a count of six.
Repeat for several rounds.
Inhale for 4 seconds, exhale for 6 to 8 seconds, and let your shoulders drop naturally when exhaling.
Sit in a sitting or semi-recumbent position, place one hand on your abdomen, and make sure your abdomen is slowly retracted when you exhale.
If you feel dizzy, shorten it to 3 inhales and 4 exhales. Stay comfortable and don’t hold your breath or pursue depth.

Case: Before the interview, he was so nervous in the corridor that his palms became sweaty. He breathed in for four seconds and exhaled for six seconds for two minutes. His shoulders slowly lowered, and his heartbeat became much more stable before entering the door.

items.title: Gradually relax your body
items.core: Tense and then relax from your feet to your head.
body: Hold each part for a few seconds.
Pay attention to how you feel after relaxing.
Press each part starting from the toes for 5 seconds, then release suddenly, and feel the soreness and swelling become lighter.
Advance in the order of calves, thighs, abdomen, shoulders and neck, and face, and make up for missed parts.
Record the body differences when relaxing. If any part is still tight, repeat two sets of that part.

Case: After working overtime, Xiao Chen still felt that his shoulders and neck were stiff while lying on the bed. He exerted force from his toes to his calves and shoulders for five seconds and then released. Before he finished, he yawned.

items.title: Set aside some mindful time
items.core: Observe the present moment without judgment.
body: Start from three minutes.
Gently pull back when your mind wanders.
Set a timer for 5 minutes. After sitting firmly, focus on the airflow at the tip of your nose or the touch on the soles of your feet.
When a thought occurs, mark it in your mind as ‘thinking’ and then return to your breathing, without pursuing content analysis.
After finishing, write a sentence about how you feel at the moment, such as ‘chest is tight’ or ‘brain slows down’.

Case: After dinner, she turned off the short video and sat by the window for ten minutes, only observing the temperature of the cup and the sound of cars downstairs, without commenting on whether she was annoyed or not, and her mood slowly calmed down.

items.title: Organize the space around you
items.core: An orderly environment can reduce the load.
body: Just tidy up a small piece.
Don’t pursue perfection.
Before going to bed, just tidy up the countertop and bedside within sight, and put the sundries into fixed storage boxes.
Use the ‘within arm’s length’ principle to clean the items at hand first, rather than rushing to tidy up the entire room.
Trash, laundry, and items to be returned are divided into three piles, and only the most conspicuous pile is processed.

Case: On Sunday morning, Xiao Wang sorted the express boxes, old receipts and charging cables on the desk, leaving only the computer and desk lamp. After sitting down, he felt refreshed and more willing to start working.

items.title: Write down your worries and categorize them
items.core: Distinguish between what you can control and what you cannot control.
body: Make a list of what you can do.
Put those that cannot be placed first.
Write ‘worries’ and ‘next steps’ on a piece of paper, with only one sentence of specific facts for each.
Circle those that can be dealt with immediately and arrange a 15-minute period for verification or communication.
If it cannot be advanced at the moment, write it to the fixed page, mark the review date next to it, and then close it.

Case: Before the deadline of the project, Amin wrote down his worries about being criticized, incomplete information, and the client’s temporary change requirements. He marked the parts that could be prepared and filled in the information first. His anxiety turned from panic to concrete actions.

items.title: Limit information intake
items.core: Bad news can amplify anxiety.
body: Set the time period for viewing news.
Do not read conflicting content before going to bed.
Turn off the news feed twice a day, and watch it for 10 minutes each during lunch break and in the evening.
Stop browsing hot searches and short videos 30 minutes before going to bed, and use paper books instead if necessary.
When you see bad news, first confirm the source and place of occurrence, and then decide whether you need to take action.

Case: Xiao Zhou had difficulty falling asleep after watching breaking news for two nights in a row. He turned off his push notifications and only read official news for ten minutes after dinner. He was no longer distracted by fragments of bad news before going to bed.

items.title: Regular diet
items.core: Blood sugar fluctuations affect mood.
body: Don’t rely on sweets to cheer you up.
Eat meals on time.
Eat breakfast within 1 hour after waking up, with protein and whole grains, and avoid drinking only coffee.
Try to keep the interval between meals at 4 to 6 hours, and prepare nuts or yogurt as a cushion when you are fasting for a long time.
Don’t overeat for dinner. If you are hungry before going to bed, eat a small amount of banana, milk or whole wheat crackers.

Case: She used to put off lunch until three o'clock in the afternoon when she was busy, and she would feel flustered and irritable in the evening; now she eats a meal and vegetables at 11:30, and her mood is much more stable when working in the afternoon.

items.title: Replenish energy with social interaction
items.core: Not all social interaction consumes energy.
body: Find someone you can relax with.
It means you just want to chat.
Prioritize appointments with people you can chat with easily and who won’t make you nervous. Limit each time to 30 to 60 minutes.
Choose to walk, eat or do crafts side by side to relax more than sitting across from each other for long periods of time.
Explain whether you want to be listened to or need advice before meeting to reduce misunderstandings and consumption.

Case: Ajie, who lives alone, was in a low mood on Saturday afternoon. He met a friend he was easy to get along with to drink coffee and chat for half an hour in the park. After returning home, he no longer felt bored and took the initiative to tidy up the room.

items.title: Retain interest time
items.core: Interest is the outlet of emotion.
body: Set aside a set amount of time each week.
Do not target output.
Fix two 30-minute blocks each week for drawing, playing the piano, doing puzzles or playing ball.
Place materials in a conspicuous place in advance to reduce the resistance of looking for things before starting.
Choose small goals that can create a sense of completion, such as completing a sketch or mastering a short paragraph.

Case: Xiao Tang worked overtime almost every day during the week to catch up with the plan, but still retained the habit of sketching for twenty minutes before going to bed; after drawing a few lines, he felt that the irritation he had suppressed had an outlet.

items.title: Only make the smallest movements when you are down
items.core: If your goal is too big, it will stop.
body: Choose something that can be done in five minutes.
No additional requirements after completion.
Narrow tasks down to actions that can be initiated in two minutes, such as opening a file, putting on your shoes, and washing a cup.
Allow yourself to do it for only five minutes first, and stop when the time is up; if you want to continue, extend it naturally, and don’t push yourself any harder.
Tick the box on the paper immediately after completion, and replace the evaluation of "I am useless today" with visible small results.

Case: She was in a very low mood on Monday night. The original plan of sorting out materials for an hour made her want to run away. She changed it to just opening the file and writing the title. She completed three lines in ten minutes and completed it the next day.

items.title: Write the problem instead of dwelling on it
items.core: Write it down and it becomes a solvable problem.
body: List known, unknown and next steps.
Break big problems into small pieces.
Take a piece of paper and write down the three repeated sentences in your mind, and then change them into questions, such as "What three points are you most afraid of in this report?"
Mark each question into three categories: verifiable, questionable, and can only wait. Deal with the items that can be verified first.
Set up a specific time slot for the smallest problem, and write down which file to open or who to contact.

Case: He repeatedly worried about making mistakes in his report while lying in bed. He took a note and wrote down "Afraid of being asked for data, afraid of forgetting words, afraid of timeout", circled the most urgent data to check, completed the form half an hour later and slept peacefully.

items.title: Don’t compete with yourself
items.core: Blaming yourself will not improve efficiency.
body: Replace "Why am I doing this" with "What should I do next time".
Give yourself and others the same tolerance.
When you find a self-blaming sentence pattern, stop for ten seconds and rewrite it into the next action, such as "Check the first paragraph first."
Replace your personality evaluation with facts. Write "I made three mistakes today" instead of "I just can't do it."
Set yourself a stop-loss time. If you are still stuck after more than 20 minutes, change methods or seek help.

Case: Xiao Zhou made a lot of mistakes in memorizing words. He originally scolded himself for being stupid, but when he saw that he still got 18 correct words that day, he changed his self-blame into a mark for wrong questions and continued to review for 20 minutes, but his efficiency stabilized.

items.title: Allow rest
items.core: Rest is not evidence of failure.
body: Schedule your breaks ahead of time rather than pushing yourself to the point of collapse.
Review the status after the break.
Write the break into the schedule and mark the start and end time to avoid endless extension and new self-blame.
Put away tools and message reminders before taking a break, so that your body can really leave the work situation.
After waking up or doing some activities, just choose a light task to restore your rhythm, such as drinking water, taking a walk, or organizing your desktop.

Case: After working overtime continuously, Xiaolin felt dizzy on Saturday afternoon. Instead of cleaning, she turned off the reminder and slept for forty minutes. When she got up, she only washed dishes and bought groceries, and no longer collapsed at night.

items.title: Resources for Hope
items.core: During lows, you need concrete evidence, not empty words.
body: Record past recovery experiences.
Watch for the little signals that are getting better.
Create an evidence folder to save thank you letters, completion screenshots, review records and specific affirmations from others.
Write down one fact every day that you have achieved, even if it is just eating on time, and mark the ability it proves.
Choose a question before reading the evidence when you are at your lowest point, and ask yourself which method you can reuse next.

Case: In the third week of unemployment, Ajie felt that he was useless, so he dug out past project emails and customer thanks, picked out three sentences of specific feedback and posted it on his desk. He was motivated to revise his resume and submit it the next day.

items.title: Lowering standards to enforceability
items.core: Perfect standards can shut down people when they are low.
body: Only completion is required, not quality.
Complete it counts.
Change the plan to the minimum version, such as reading only two pages when reading and only warming up for five minutes when exercising.
Bind the location with the action. When you get to the desk, write a line. When you get to the door, go downstairs and walk around.
No punitive tasks will be added after completion, and the standards will be slightly raised after stabilization for three consecutive days.

Case: Xiao Chen wanted to resume exercise after falling out of love. He originally planned to run five kilometers a day but gave up. He changed his standard to changing shoes and walking downstairs for ten minutes. After four consecutive days, his physical strength recovered and he increased it to jogging.

items.title: One thing at a time
items.core: Too many choices can make you feel powerless.
body: Write down the only thing you have to do.
After you finish, think about the next thing.
Close redundant tabs before starting, put your phone away, and leave only the materials for the current task.
Use a piece of paper to write down the only goal for this round. Do not add new tasks or check other lists before completing it.
If you think of something else, write it down in the to-do area next to it and wait until the current twenty-five minutes are over before dealing with it.

Case: There were many tasks at night. Xiao Zhao opened five windows at the same time. The more he looked at it, the more panicked he became. He closed the other windows and only finished writing the bill page. He settled the expenses in 20 minutes, and his anxiety dropped significantly.

items.title: Record completions rather than feelings
items.core: Feelings can be deceiving, recordings cannot.
body: Write down the next thing you accomplished.
Read it before going to bed.
Write three completed facts every day before going to bed, starting with a verb, such as pay, reply, organize, and go out.
The record only records the behavior and quantity, without evaluating the quality or bad, to avoid turning the check-in into a new criticism.
When you feel down, read the last seven records first, and then decide which little thing you can make up for that day.

Case: Before the depression review, Xiao Min felt that she had done nothing this week. She opened the punch card and saw that bathing, buying medicine, and replying to messages were all checked. She admitted that she was maintaining her life and felt a little more relaxed.

items.title: Find someone to talk to
items.core: You don’t have to wait until you are in good shape to speak.
body: Indicate whether you want to be listened to or helped.
Allow the other person not to know how to answer.
First make a fixed opening sentence, such as "I'm not feeling well today, can you listen to me for ten minutes?"
Only talk about one topic when talking about things, express them in the order of facts, feelings, and needs, and do not require the other party to solve everything.
If it is difficult to speak in person, you can use voice or text instead, and make an appointment at a specific time to avoid waiting for a reply.

Case: Xiao He didn’t want to talk during the lunch break, but he still sent a message to his friend, “I’m having a bad day today.” The other party responded with a voice message. He cried for a while and was able to return to work in the afternoon to deal with minor matters.

items.title: Avoid major decisions
items.core: Judgment is prone to bias during low times.
body: Delay the decision until the state is restored.
Handle daily affairs first.
Set a 24-hour cooling-off period for resignations, breakups, and large purchases, and only collect facts during this period.
Write the decision into two columns: immediate emotional reasons and verifiable consequences, and then see which column has the evidence.
Consult someone who knows the situation first, ask for the minimum trial and error plan, and don’t rush to make irreversible choices.

Case: Xiao Liu wanted to resign immediately after the quarrel. He saved the draft of his resignation in a folder and agreed to sleep for two nights before talking about it. After calming down the next day, he changed it to meeting with his supervisor to discuss job changes first to avoid impulsive decisions.

items.title: 保留日常节律
items.core: 吃饭睡觉出门是底座。
body: Restore the most basic rhythm first.
Do not pursue additional goals.
First fix three anchor points: getting up, lunch, and going to bed, and then fine-tune the rest of the arrangements around these three points.
Choose simple, ready-made foods for each meal, and prepare water and medicine to reduce the burden of decision-making when energy is low.
Go out and bask in the sun for ten minutes every day or stand by the window to allow your body to receive day and night signals.

Case: Xiao Wang took a leave of absence at home due to a low fever. He did not force himself to study. He only ate breakfast on time, basked in the sun, took out the trash, and went to bed on time at night. After three days, his work and rest were not messed up, and it was easier to return to work.

items.title: Reduce being alone for long periods of time
items.core: Being alone can amplify rumination.
body: Go where there are people.
No need to socialize, just stay.
Cut your alone time into segments of no more than two hours, and then go for a walk downstairs or move to a public space.
Give low-cost options when making a date, such as walking together, making a short phone call, or doing separate things in a coffee shop.
Prepare a list of three places to go: the library, community center, and park. When you feel down, just go out.

Case: When Xiao Tang was alone on weekends, he kept thinking about old things. He brought water and went to the community library to sit for an hour, attended the reading group and greeted the store clerk. He returned home with less rumination.

items.title: 不要用酒精助眠
items.core: 它会破坏睡眠结构。
body: Short-term relaxation is exchanged for long-term fluctuations.
Seek alternatives when needed.
Stop drinking alcohol four hours before going to bed and drink warm water instead. If you rely on alcohol to fall asleep, record your consumption for a week before seeking medical advice.
Use your bedroom only for sleeping. Get up if you can't fall asleep in twenty minutes, do some quiet reading and then go back to bed.
If your hand tremors, palpitation, or insomnia worsen after quitting drinking, don’t force yourself to do it, and see a doctor as soon as possible to adjust your plan.

Case: Xiao Zhou relied on red wine to fall asleep for several days after falling out of love. He fell asleep quickly at first, but woke up frequently in the second half of the night. His dizziness during the day affected his work. She stopped drinking before bed and consulted her doctor about a sleep plan. After a week, her sleep became more stable.

items.title: 给自己一段时间
items.core: 恢复不是一瞬间的事。
body: No short deadlines.
Repetitions allowed.
Set up a two-week observation period and record emotional scores at the same time every day. Don't rush to draw conclusions based on single-day fluctuations.
Reduce the goal to something executable, such as spending ten minutes in the sun every day, taking a bath, and eating a hot meal.
Agree a re-evaluation date in advance and check whether your sleep, appetite, and energy have improved slightly compared to the starting point.

Case: In the third week of unemployment, A Lan still cried after submitting two resumes every day. She no longer forced herself to cheer up immediately, and only stipulated that she should deal with job applications in the morning and take a half-hour walk in the afternoon. Six weeks later, she began to stabilize in interviews and her mood slowly returned.

items.title: Looking Back at Recovery
items.core: Evidence is more helpful than encouragement.
body: Write down your experience of coming out.
Refining the actions that were effective at the time.
Draw out your diary or chat history from previous periods of depression and find out the specific behaviors that first improved at that time.
Make a list: the method that worked last time, the time it took, the people who helped, and the parts that can be reused this time.
Write three things that have improved in the past in three lines, and put them in the memo on your phone for review when you are at a low point.

Case: Xiao Chen always said he was useless when he was depressed. When he was looking through old notes, he saw that during the same insomnia days last year, he went from going out for five minutes a day to running again, and recovered after two months. He took a photo of that page and saved it, regaining his patience.

items.title: Look for small signals
items.core: Changes often appear in the little things first.
body: Watch your sleep and appetite.
Record small improvements.
Record small things such as taking a shower, replying to messages, and taking out the trash when you go out. If you complete it for three consecutive days, it will be a noteworthy change.
Pay attention to whether the time it takes to wake up in the morning shortens, or the number of sighs decreases. These changes occur earlier than the mood score.
Take a photo of your window sill or desktop every week to use the changes in your environment to remind yourself that you don’t have to wait for a big turnaround.

Case: Xiaomei didn’t go out for a whole week. One day she found herself sunbathing on the balcony, replying to friends' messages, and throwing away takeout boxes. As she wrote these things down, she realized that changes started with these little things, rather than suddenly getting better.

items.title: Get a professional evaluation
items.core: Persistent depression deserves to be taken seriously.
body: Record duration and impact.
Consult a professional.
If you feel depressed or have significant changes in sleep or appetite for two consecutive weeks, make an appointment with a psychiatric or psychological clinic.
Write down the time of onset of illness, family history, medications, thoughts of self-harm, and degree of impact on daily functioning before your visit.
In the first consultation, you can directly ask about the diagnosis, severity, treatment plan and follow-up time, and avoid just chatting.

Case: Xiao Liu woke up early for two consecutive weeks, lost appetite, and did not want to see anyone on weekends. He made an appointment with a psychiatrist and brought a recorded sleep and mood chart. After the doctor completed the interview and scale, he worked with him to develop a review and intervention plan.

items.title: Prepare crisis plans
items.core: The worst times also require plans.
body: Write down people you can contact.
Save Crisis Hotline.
Write down three people who can be contacted immediately and their phone numbers. Note who can answer the phone at night or accompany you to the doctor.
Save the contact information of emergency departments, local psychological assistance hotlines and attending doctors in advance and put them on the homepage of your mobile phone.
When in an emotional state, give large quantities of drugs and potentially harmful items to a trusted person and leave the solitude.

Case: Aning was in a hurry on the most uncomfortable night. Later, she put emergency contacts, help hotlines and a list of commonly used medicines on the homepage of her mobile phone, and gave dangerous items to friends for safekeeping. When an emotional storm hit, she asked for help according to the list and got through it safely.

items.title: Speak out feelings rather than accuse
items.core: "I feel..." is more effective than "You always...".
body: Describe specific behavior.
Make a clear request.
Start with "I feel uneasy because..." and then talk about a specific scenario. Don't judge the other person's current motives first.
Change the question sentence into a demand sentence, such as "You didn't reply to the message" to "I need to be informed in time."
After the conversation, ask the other party what point they understood. If you go off track, just add "What I care about most is...".

Case: My partner came home late for three consecutive days. Xiaodou did not say "you always ignore me", but said "I feel uneasy waiting for you and hope to know the arrangements in advance". The other party put down his cell phone to explain working overtime, and the two agreed to send messages before returning home late, and the quarrels subsided.

items.title: You don’t have to be responsible for everyone
items.core: Boundaries are a prerequisite for a long-term relationship.
body: Clear whose problem should be solved by whom.
Assess your own capabilities before helping.
First clarify whose task it is: who raises the issue, who bears the consequences, and who has the ability to decide.
Ask before helping, "Do you want me to listen, give you advice, or help you deal with it?" Only agree to one of them.
When the other party repeatedly puts the blame on you, end it with "I can only do this" and give a time point.

Case: Colleagues often push temporary reports to Xiao Fang, and she also works overtime until late at night. Later, she only took over the data she was responsible for, listed the rest on the handover form and stated the time. My colleagues were not used to it at first, but after a few times they learned to make arrangements in advance.

items.title: Comparison steals satisfaction
items.core: Other people’s progress is not your yardstick.
body: Reduce exposure to comparison scenarios.
Use your last time as a reference.
When you see other people’s progress, close the page and write down a small thing you completed today before continuing.
Change the reference object to yourself three months ago, and only look at one of sleep, exercise, work or savings.
Cancel account reminders that easily trigger anxiety, set a fifteen-minute countdown for browsing, and leave at that point.

Case: After Xiao Lin browsed the friend circle of a classmate who got promoted, he felt that his year had been in vain and he couldn't even find the energy to celebrate his small goals. She turned off the dynamic reminder, looked at her schedule again, and found that she had completed two certificate exams in three months.

items.title: Social support is a real resource
items.core: You don’t have to carry it all alone.
body: Say what specific help you need.
Also allow yourself to be taken care of.
List three types of people: those who can listen, those who can provide information, and those who can accompany you to do things. Mark their contact information respectively.
When asking a friend for help, state the time and method, such as "Can you walk with me for twenty minutes after dinner on Wednesday?"
After receiving help, reply with a specific thank you and tell the other person what was useful so that they can continue to help next time.

Case: On the day of moving, boxes were piled up in the living room, and Xiao Xu sat alone until the evening without finishing unpacking them. She sent a message for help to two friends, who brought self-adhesive bags and tape and cleaned up the kitchen and bedroom in two hours. She ate well for the first time that night.

items.title: Recognize signs that you need professional help
items.core: If it persists, is severe, or affects your functionality, you should seek help.
body: Be aware of your sleep, appetite, and daily functions.
Ask for help immediately if you have any crisis thoughts.
When your depression lasts for more than two weeks and is difficult to relieve most of the time, you should make an appointment for evaluation as soon as possible.
If there are more mistakes in work and study, avoidance of social interactions, and difficulty in washing, it means that daily operation has been significantly hindered.
When you have thoughts of not wanting to live, harming yourself, or obviously losing control, contact your doctor or a trusted person on the same day.

Case: Xiao Tang was depressed for nearly a month. He was late three times in a row and delayed submitting his reports. Instead of just trying to persuade him to be happy, his friend accompanied him to the psychological clinic. After the evaluation, it was found that the symptoms had affected his work, so he began to review and adjust his work and rest according to the doctor's instructions.

items.title: Be specific in your request
items.core: A vague request makes it difficult for others to start.
body: Describe what is needed and how long it will take.
Give the other party room to refuse.
Describe the object, thing, time and method, such as "Please accompany me to sort out materials for ten minutes at eight o'clock tonight."
First tell whether the other party can do it, and then give room for withdrawal, such as "It's okay if it's inconvenient, I'll ask other people first."
After speaking, confirm the details: when to meet, where, and what needs to be done to avoid inconsistent understanding between the two parties.

Case: A colleague always asked Xiao Zhou to "do a favor" temporarily. Xiao Zhou agreed after asking clearly which page of the PPT was to be changed, what time it was sent before, and whether charts were needed. The other party quickly let go, and Xiao Zhou was able to arrange his time without having to work overtime due to speculation.

items.title: Accept help
items.core: There is no need to feel guilty about being cared for.
body: Say something specific that can help.
Feedback the results afterwards.
When someone hands you water, offers a seat, or helps with something, say "thank you" first and then take it. Don't rush to explain that you are already prepared.

When a friend offers to pick you up or accompany you to a doctor, state the time and location directly, and ask the other person what is convenient for you to avoid being so polite that the information is unclear.

Write down the small things that others have done for you, and then take the initiative to respond when the other person needs it; the reward can be companionship, and there is no need to settle on the spot.

Case: When Zhou Xiaoya had a cold, she had to catch up on the plan, and a friend took the initiative to bring porridge and medicine. She repeatedly said "no need to bother" at first, then took the lunch box and made an appointment to treat her friends to tea next time. After receiving care, she discovered that she owed nothing to anyone.

items.title: 拒绝后不要内疚
items.core: 拒绝不等于否定对方。
body: Explain your limitations.
No additional explanation.

When rejecting an invitation, first say "I won't go this time" and then explain the reasons and blessings. Do not repeatedly foreshadow the invitation, and do not make additional promises of compensation.
Keep the same sentence when the other party presses the question, such as "I need to rest on the weekend." Don't be dragged into bargaining by explaining too much.
Saying no is definitely not the right person. You can add "I'll make an appointment next time when I'm free", but only say it when you are really willing to avoid causing misunderstandings.

Case: A friend invited Xiao Lin to move at the weekend. Xiao Lin had to take care of a child with a fever that day, so he said, "I can't come, but I will give you a bottle of water." The friend expressed understanding, Xiaolin did not explain repeatedly, and the relationship did not become estranged.

items.title: 边界要提前说
items.core: 等冲突爆发再说就晚了。
body: When you are calm, explain how you can help.
Start with "I can".
Make the agreement clear at the beginning about the time, location and how long you can participate, for example, "I have to leave at 8:30, and I will not renew the stall later."

For requests such as borrowing money, working as a substitute, or temporarily adding work, give a fixed message in advance: "I generally don't borrow large amounts of money" and "I don't accept work on weekday evenings."

Before entering into a relationship or cooperation, explain the unacceptable methods, such as not checking your cell phone, not talking about business late at night, and not changing the deadline at short notice.

Case: When Amin first started accepting private manuscripts, he stated that he would only make two revisions, and there would be an extra fee for any more revisions. Later, the client frequently revised the draft, and she reminded her as agreed, and the other party accepted it calmly; if she waited until the fifth edition to make changes, both parties would feel aggrieved.

items.title: 少用指责句式
items.core: 「你总是」会立刻激起防御。
body: Describe the specific behavior this time.
Say how you feel.
Replace "Why did you forget again" with "I saw that the form has not been updated yet. What time should we complete it before?" Let's talk about the facts first and then the needs.
When making requests, add specific scenarios and criteria, such as "Send me the information ten minutes before the meeting." Don't comment on the other person's personality.
Stop for ten seconds when you get emotional, and just describe your feelings and consequences: "I'm a little panicked now, afraid that I won't be able to submit in time."

Case: The husband forgot to take out the trash again. The wife did not say "You always don't care about anything", but said "I am very tired today, I hope you take the trash out now." He did it immediately, and the two did not quarrel.

items.title: 冲突后尝试修复
items.core: No cold war is the bottom line.
body: 说清你在意什么。
Use actions to show your willingness to continue.
Send a brief confirmation within 24 hours after the quarrel: "The tone was harsh just now, I want to make things clear." Let's cool down first and don't argue about winning or losing.

When resuming the negotiation, only choose one issue that you want to solve the most, and talk about the process according to the timeline, so as to avoid bringing up old accounts and speculation together.
If the other party doesn’t want to talk for the time being, agree on a specific time to talk again, and stop being cold-faced, sarcastic, and blocking before then.

Case: After Xiao Wang had an argument with his colleagues over differences in plans, he took the initiative to send a message to his colleagues after get off work and said, "I'm getting impatient today. Let's go over our ideas together tomorrow?" The colleague responded and agreed to discuss it the next day, so we didn't fall into a cold war.

items.title: Not responsible for others
items.core: Clear whose problem should be solved by whom.
body: 帮忙前估自己的余力。
不接管对方的选择。
When the other party forgets to bring his ID, you can provide a reminder or accompany him to find it, but you cannot make up excuses for him to teachers, clients or family members.
If your colleague fails to submit the materials on time, you can send a reminder and copy the progress. Do not fill in the entire report for him late at night.
The judgment standard is: Whose behavior is mainly responsible for the consequences and who has the ability to remedy the situation will be the first to propose a plan.

Case: Lao Zhang’s relatives borrowed money for turnover, and Lao Zhang lent money despite knowing that he often gambled. Later, his relatives were unable to repay and pestered him many times, so Lao Zhang clearly refused to help anymore, and each of them had to bear the financial consequences.

items.title: Pause when comparing
items.core: Other people’s progress is not your yardstick.
body: Reduce exposure to comparison scenarios.
Use your last time as a reference.
When you see a classmate getting promoted or a friend buying a house, close the page and write down three small things you accomplished this week, and then decide whether to continue reading.
Divide other people’s achievements into conditions: resources, time, city, family support, and then set your own goals after seeing the differences clearly.
Set review boundaries for yourself, for example, only review your progress once a week, and sleep, study, and rest as planned the rest of the time.

Case: Xiao He learned that his classmate was promoted to supervisor in two years, and he was so anxious that he couldn't sleep. Later, she temporarily muted her circle of friends and prepared for certificate exams and gained experience at her own pace. After half a year, she successfully changed jobs, only to realize that comparison cannot replace action.

items.title: Save energy when socializing
items.core: Not all invitations must be accepted.
body: 按当前精力选择。
Politely refuse.

When receiving a party invitation, first check the calendar and your physical strength that day. If there is a morning meeting the next day, reply "I won't go this time. Make an appointment in advance next time."
Set a budget for others, such as two meetings a week and one long online chat. After that, only participate in necessary activities.
After arriving at the venue, set a departure time for yourself, tell your companions in advance "I'm leaving at nine o'clock", and just leave quietly at that time.

Case: A colleague organized a bureau singing on Friday night. Ajie has worked overtime for three consecutive days this week and only replied, "I won't go this time. We will meet at lunch next time." He didn't make up excuses, was in better shape on Monday after a break, and didn't lose friends.

items.title: 说明自己的状态
items.core: 别人无法读心。
body: 告诉亲近的人你最近累了。
说出需要的支持。
When you are busy or feeling down, give a clear message to those close to you: "I'm having a bad day today. I want to stay quiet tonight and we'll talk tomorrow."
When you need support, say specific actions, such as "accompany me to register at the hospital" or "help me read my resume for ten minutes." Don't just say that I am tired.

Update in a timely manner when the situation changes. For example, if you originally promised to go to an appointment but can't keep it, you should say it two hours in advance and don't disappear temporarily.

Case: Xiao Tang returned home after surgery, and her family thought she could do housework normally. She directly said, "I am out of breath after walking for ten minutes now. Please make a simple dinner first, and I will wash the dishes later." After her family understood this, they adjusted the arrangement, and she was relieved of a lot of grievances.

items.title: Understand the channels for help
items.core: Find them quickly when needed.
body: 保存咨询和热线信息。
知道去哪里就医。
Save frequently used numbers in your mobile phone: family members, neighbors, community properties, school hospitals or company personnel, and name them according to the scene.
Check the nearby emergency rooms, psychological hotlines, legal aid and police methods in advance, and write down the addresses, opening hours and required materials.
Put important documents, insurance policies, and medical records in an encrypted album so that they can be sent out immediately when you contact professionals.

Case: Aunt Li usually keeps the community police, property maintenance and children's phone numbers at the top of her mobile phone. When a water pipe bursts at home, she quickly contacts the repair team and solves the leak in half an hour.

items.title: Ask for help immediately in times of crisis
items.core: Don’t bear the responsibility alone.
body: 联系可信的人陪伴。
拨打热线或就医。
When you have thoughts of self-harm, are threatened, or are at risk of losing contact, call the local emergency number immediately and do not wait until your mood stabilizes.
At the same time, contact someone who can be present and say directly, "I'm not safe right now. Please come right away or call the police for me." Don't just send an emoji.
Send the location, characteristics of the other party, and time of occurrence to relatives and friends, keep the call or location sharing, and try to go to public areas.

Case: Xiao Chen came home late at night and found that he was being followed. He immediately ran into the convenience store and dialed 110. He also contacted his friends. The police quickly arrived to deal with the matter and Xiao Chen got home safely.

items.title: 遭遇骚扰保留证据
items.core: Taking screenshots and recording is important.
body: Save the original information.
Seek platform or legal help.
After receiving harassment messages, take a screenshot of the complete conversation, including account number, time, date and platform name, and then block or report it.
To deal with phone harassment, use call records and recording to record the number, frequency and specific content of the calls. Be careful to save the original files.
When being followed or entangled offline, write down the location, clothing and people traveling with you, save clues to the monitoring location, and call the police if necessary.

Case: Xiao Liu received multiple vulgar WeChat harassments from his colleagues. He took screenshots one by one and saved the content with time. He later submitted the evidence when he complained to the company’s HR. HR interviewed the harasser and gave him a warning.
